contents.name: Section 2.2: local causality inside a normal neighborhood, the exponential cone and the displacement-length bound
contents.support: The theorem proves that causal reachability inside a convex normal ball is the exponential cone, that the Lorentzian length is bounded by the displacement radius and that null endpoints force the null geodesic, with supporting lemmas on the position-vector differential and length monotonicity.

contents.name: Theorem 2.12 and Definition 2.16: locally Lipschitz parametrization of continuous causal curves and inextendibility
contents.support:
Current local carrier Statement scope for owner source-coverage reconciliation:

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], [[def-gr-metric-selected-connection]]).
Call a map $x:I\to M$ a **geodesically connectible continuous causal curve**
when it is continuous ([[def-continuity-real]]) and for every strictly convex
normal ball $C$ as produced by [[thm-gr-convex-normal-neighborhoods]]
([[def-gr-normal-neighborhoods-and-position-vectors]] clause (b)) and all
$t_1<t_2$ in $I$ with $x([t_1,t_2])\subseteq C$, the endpoints $x(t_1)$ and
$x(t_2)$ are joined by a future causal geodesic whose image is contained in
$C$. Write $\le$ for the causal relation of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] (defined by locally absolutely
continuous future causal curves) and put
$$n:=\frac{N}{\sqrt{-g(N,N)}},\qquad h:=g+2\,n^\flat\otimes n^\flat .$$

**(a) Absolutely continuous implies connectible.** Every future causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ in the sense of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] is a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve.

**(b) Connectible curves give causal relations.** Let $x:I\to M$ be a
geodesically connectible continuous causal curve and let $t_1<t_2$ in $I$.
Then for every open neighborhood $W$ of $x([t_1,t_2])$ there is a piecewise
smooth future causal curve $\eta:[t_1,t_2]\to W$ with $\eta(t_1)=x(t_1)$ and
$\eta(t_2)=x(t_2)$ (in particular a locally absolutely continuous future
causal curve, so $x(t_1)\le x(t_2)$ in the relation defined by
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]).

**(c) Equality of relations.** For $p,q\in M$ the following are equivalent:
$p\le q$; $p=q$ or there is a geodesically connectible continuous causal
curve with endpoints $p,q$.

**(d) One-sided extension.** Let $\gamma:[0,\infty)\to M$ be a
future-inextendible future causal curve in the sense of
[[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]] clause (d). Then there is an
inextendible future causal curve $\gamma^*:I^*\to M$ with
$[0,\infty)\subseteq I^*\subseteq\mathbb R$ and $\gamma^*|_{[0,\infty)}=\gamma$;
that is, $\gamma$ is contained in a curve that is both future- and
past-inextendible. The dual statement holds for past-inextendible curves.

No choice principle is used. The extension in (d) is not asserted to be
unique.

Exact local scope projection only; authoritative source fidelity and full consumer acceptance remain GR owner duties.

contents.name: Theorem 4.119 and the volume-function proof (continuous strictly increasing time function with Cauchy levels)
contents.support:
Current local carrier Statement scope for owner source-coverage reconciliation:

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice
([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]) for the curve calculus and auxiliary-length suppliers. Let $(M,g,N)$ be a globally hyperbolic
time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause (c)) and let
$\mu$ be the volume measure of [[lem-gr-finite-smooth-volume-density]] with
$\mu(M)=1$, $\mu(O)>0$ for every nonempty open $O$ and $\mu(E)=0$ for every
chart-Lebesgue-null Borel set. Let $L:=\ln$ denote the natural logarithm
([[def-natural-logarithm]]) and define the **volume time function**
$$t:M\longrightarrow\mathbb R,\qquad t(p):=L\bigl(\mu(I^-(p))\bigr)-L\bigl(\mu(I^+(p))\bigr) =\ln\frac{\mu(I^-(p))}{\mu(I^+(p))}.$$
Then:

**(a)** $t$ is well defined and continuous on $M$;

**(b)** $t$ is strictly increasing along causal relations: if $p\le q$
with $p\ne q$, then $t(p)<t(q)$; in particular $t$ is a time function in
the sense of [[def-gr-causal-conditions-and-global-hyperbolicity]] clause
(d);

**(c)** for every inextendible future-directed causal curve
$\gamma:I\to M$ one has
$$\lim_{s\to\sup I}t(\gamma(s))=+\infty,\qquad \lim_{s\to\inf I}t(\gamma(s))=-\infty;$$

**(d)** every level set $t^{-1}(c)$, $c\in\mathbb R$, is a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)); in
particular it is acausal, and it is met in exactly one parameter value by
every inextendible causal curve.

No smoothness of $t$ is asserted.

Exact local scope projection only; authoritative source fidelity and full consumer acceptance remain GR owner duties.

contents.name: Section 3.1-3.3: domains of dependence, Cauchy horizons and global properties of Cauchy sets
contents.support:
Current local carrier Statement scope for owner source-coverage reconciliation:

Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold
([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]) and let $S\subseteq M$ be a Cauchy set
([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]] clause (c)): every
inextendible causal curve $\gamma:I\to M$ has
$\gamma^{-1}[S]=\{t\in I:\gamma(t)\in S\}$ of exactly one element. Then:

**(a)** there is no nonconstant future causal curve $\delta:[a,b]\to M$
with $\delta(a)=\delta(b)$; in particular $S$ is achronal and acausal, and
the three sets $I^-(S)$, $S$, $I^+(S)$ are pairwise disjoint with
$$M=I^-(S)\;\sqcup\;S\;\sqcup\;I^+(S);$$
moreover for $x\notin S$ one has $x\in I^+(S)$ if and only if some point of
$S$ chronologically precedes $x$;

**(b)** $S$ is closed in $M$;

**(c)** for every $p\in S$ there are a chart $(U,x)$ of the kind produced by
[[lem-gr-dominating-cone-bounds]] clauses (a) and (d) around $p$, with
$x(p)=0$ and the supplier constants $K\ge1$ and $c=16$, and numbers $a,\rho,\eta>0$ with $\sqrt c\,\rho+\eta<a$ and
$W:=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times B_\rho(0)\bigr)\subseteq U$ such that for every
$z\in B_\rho(0)$ the coordinate vertical line
$L_z=x^{-1}\bigl((-a,a)\times\{z\}\bigr)$ meets $S\cap W$ in exactly one
point $x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$, and
$$|\varphi(z)-\varphi(z')|\le\sqrt c\,|z-z'|\qquad(z,z'\in B_\rho(0)),$$
with $\varphi(0)=0$ and $|\varphi(z)|\le\sqrt c\,|z|<a$. The cylinder $W$ may be chosen inside any prescribed neighborhood of $p$. Consequently the maps
$z\mapsto x^{-1}(\varphi(z),z)$ form a topological atlas on the closed set
$S$, making $S$ a topological $3$-manifold in the subspace topology whose
inclusion into $M$ is a topological embedding.

Exact local scope projection only; authoritative source fidelity and full consumer acceptance remain GR owner duties.

contents.name: Application of the splitting to the existence of Cauchy hypersurfaces
contents.support:
Current local carrier Statement scope for owner source-coverage reconciliation:

Assume Countable Choice and Dependent Choice ([[def-countable-choice]], [[def-dependent-choice]]). Let $(M,g,N)$ be a time-oriented smooth Lorentzian four-manifold ([[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]]), with the locally absolutely continuous causal curves of [[def-gr-causal-curves-and-reachability]]. Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval containing $0$, and let $B_R\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be the open ball of radius $R>0$ centered at $0$, with Euclidean norm $|\cdot|$. Suppose $(s,\sigma):U\to I\times B_R$ is a diffeomorphism of an open set $U\subseteq M$, satisfying:

**(C1)** $\partial_s$ is future timelike and every $s$-level is spacelike;

**(C2)** there is $K\ge1$ such that $|d\sigma(v)|\le Kds(v)$ for every nonzero future causal vector $v$ based in $U$.

Write $S=s^{-1}(0)$, and compute the domains of dependence intrinsically in $U$:
$$D^+_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every past-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\},\qquad D^-_U(S)=\{p\in U:\text{every future-inextendible causal curve in }U\text{ through }p\text{ meets }S\}.$$
Here inextendibility means absence of an endpoint limit in the specified open submanifold, and Cauchy intersection means exactly one parameter visit ([[def-gr-spacelike-hypersurfaces-and-cauchy-sets]]). Then:

**(a)** $D^+_U(S)\subseteq\{s\ge0\}$ and $D^-_U(S)\subseteq\{s\le0\}$.

**(b)** The corrected open collar
$$Q=\{q\in U:|\sigma(q)|+K|s(q)|<R\}$$
is a neighborhood of the entire slice $S$ in $U$ and is contained in $D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S)$; more precisely $Q\cap\{s>0\}\subseteq D^+_U(S)$ and $Q\cap\{s<0\}\subseteq D^-_U(S)$.

**(c)** The open set $W=\operatorname{int}_U(D^+_U(S)\cup D^-_U(S))$ contains $Q$, and $S$ is a Cauchy hypersurface of $(W,g|_W,N|_W)$. Consequently $W$ is globally hyperbolic by [[thm-gr-cauchy-surface-implies-globally-hyperbolic]].

**(d) Generic spacelike and noncompact scope.** For every smooth embedded spacelike hypersurface $\Sigma\subseteq M$ without boundary there exist an open neighborhood $U_\Sigma$ of $\Sigma$, a smooth positive function $\delta:\Sigma\to(0,\infty)$, and a diffeomorphism
$$F:\Omega\to U_\Sigma,\qquad\Omega=\{(s,x)\in\mathbb R\times\Sigma:|s|<\delta(x)\},\qquad F(0,x)=x,$$
such that $s$ is temporal and $F_*\partial_s$ is future timelike. The intrinsic set $W_\Sigma=\operatorname{int}_{U_\Sigma}(D^+_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma)\cup D^-_{U_\Sigma}(\Sigma))$ is an open neighborhood in which $\Sigma$ is Cauchy, hence is globally hyperbolic. Neither compactness nor global acausality of $\Sigma$ in $M$ is assumed. No positive uniform lower bound for $\delta$ is asserted.

Exact local scope projection only; authoritative source fidelity and full consumer acceptance remain GR owner duties.

alternatives.argument: The convexity statement is proved in the item from the coordinate geodesic equation: for f(s):=|x(γ(s))|²_e one has f″=2|ẋ|²_e−2x·Γ(x)[ẋ,ẋ]≥0 on a small coordinate ball, hence no interior maximum for f. Chrusciel, Elements of causality theory, arXiv:1110.6706, Proposition 2.2.6 with complete proof (pp. 12-13) proves the same statement from the same displayed estimate, and Minguzzi, Lorentzian causality theory, Theorem 2.4 (p. 26-27) states the coordinate-ball form of strict convexity; both sources are fetch-verified in this coverage file.

The two-sided speed bounds follow from the coordinate geodesic equation and the differential inequality w′≤‖Γ‖_K w² (with cor-bounded-derivative-implies-lipschitz and thm-ftc-second-part), which the item proves in full. Chrusciel's Proposition 2.2.6 proof contains the same local second-derivative estimate bounding a geodesic by its initial data in a small ball, and Minguzzi's Theorem 2.4 convexity argument is the second independent treatment.

The strict-convexity theorem is authored locally; its convexity kernel is lem-gr-coordinate-ball-geodesic-convexity together with the joint exponential diffeomorphism of thm-gr-local-geodesics-and-exponential-map. The independent treatments are Minguzzi, Definition 2.3 and Theorem 2.4 (pp. 26-27), and Chrusciel, Sections 2.2-2.3 with Propositions 2.2.3 and 2.2.6 (pp. 10-13).

The construction h′=(1+|df|_h²)h with a proper exhausting f and the completeness of each component are proved in the item; the residual closed-bounded-compact step is the Hopf-Rinow equivalence. Minguzzi, section 1.6 with Theorem 1.5 (pp. 10-11) records the conformal-class completion and the Hopf-Rinow compactness of closed balls, and Lemma 2.17 (pp. 33-34) the unbounded-arclength counterpart; that article is fetch-verified in this coverage file.
